cases.id: delete a key from a packed single-line struct (regression)
cases.note: Regression: a compact single-line struct packs multiple fields onto one physical line, so `deleteKey`'s generic line-based delete used to remove the whole line. ZON compounds this: a field's key span starts at the bare identifier, not its leading `.` (its declared `key_sigil`; see `insertFlowMapEntry`), so the comma-aware flow-splice fallback must also back up over that `.` itself, or it strands a bare `.` next to the surviving sibling instead of removing the field cleanly.

cases.id: delete first key of a packed single-line struct
remove the only item of a tuple leaves .{}
cases.note: An emptied tuple is `.{}`, which ZON reads as an empty struct, the one literal for both: the delete guard counts that as the tuple emptied, not as a value changing kind.

cases.id: delete a field after a multi-line string leaves the string alone
cases.note: The line after a multi-line string's last `\\` line belongs to the string, and the splice that deleted `.c` with the comma before it joined the rest of `c`'s line onto it. A field that begins its line goes with the comma after it (docs/tasks/delete-splices-taking-other-values.md).

cases.id: delete only key of a single-field struct (regression)
cases.note: Regression: deleting the *only* field of a single-field struct must leave an empty struct `.{}`, not delete the braces with the line. The `.`-backup of the flow splice must still fire so no bare `.` is stranded.

cases.id: delete last key of a multi-line struct (regression)
cases.note: Regression: deleting the *last* field of a one-field-per-line struct used to strand the predecessor's separator comma before the closing brace.

cases.id: array append/prepend/remove
appendValue on an empty .{} is NotASequence (ZON has no way to tell an empty struct from an empty array)
cases.note: Zig error NotASequence. Unlike JSON's `[]`/`{}` or YAML's `[]`/`{}`, ZON's struct and array literals share one empty spelling (`.{}`); fig's parser resolves that ambiguity by always treating an empty container as a mapping (see `zon/parser.zig`'s "empty .{} is an empty mapping" test). So there is no ZON source an empty *array* append could target — the caller must seed a non-empty array (or a struct) explicitly.

cases.id: appendValue starts an absent list as .{}, which its first item makes a tuple
cases.note: Zig error NotASequence. The seed is the same `.{}` the test above cannot append to; what `setAppend` wrote it as is a list, and the item goes in as one. An empty struct that was there is real data, and is not taken for one. `setAppend` on a list that is there, or on a value that is not a list, is `appendToSeq`'s own append or refusal, which is the binding's `appendValue`.

cases.id: replace an enum-literal value with another kind
cases.note: An enum literal's span covers its leading `.`, so a replace takes the whole literal; it used to splice past the dot and leave it in front of the new text, turning `true` into the enum literal `.true`.

setTrailingComment on a CRLF line goes before the CR
cases.note: A CRLF line's content ends before its CR: a new trailing comment goes there, and the line keeps its CRLF. Spliced after the CR, it read back in YAML as the string "1\r".

cases.id: setTrailingComment refuses a ZON multiline string's line [1]
cases.note: Zig error CommentInsideValue. A ZON `\\` line is string text up to its newline, so there is no place on it for a comment: one appended there parsed, as part of the string. The edit is refused and rolled back, LF or CRLF.
